article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies
Breeder: Barney’s Farm
THC Content: Up to approximately 30%
CBD Content: Generally low
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , Limonene , Humulene
Primary Flavors: Sweet berries, mint chocolate, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 65–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: First to second week of October
Indoor Yield: 650–750 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Up to 1,500–2,000 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Gelato #45 occupies an unusual place in modern cannabis: familiar enough to carry the famous Gelato name, yet earthy and pine-driven enough to stand apart from the sweeter versions that made the family famous. Break apart a mature flower and creamy berry sweetness can quickly give way to mint, citrus peel, damp soil, pepper, and resinous pine. That contrast makes the cultivar feel more substantial than a straightforward dessert weed. Its effects follow the same pattern. The opening is often sociable, euphoric, and playful, while the experience slowly gains physical weight without immediately shutting down mental activity. For consumers attracted to Gelato genetics but looking for something less sugary and more grounded, this selection provides a particularly interesting interpretation of the family.
Genetics and Lineage

The documented Barney’s Farm version comes from Sunset Sherbet crossed with Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies. The breeder describes its selection as a 60% indica, 40% sativa hybrid capable of reaching approximately 30% THC, with a flowering cycle of 65–70 days. Those parents place the plant squarely within the genetic framework associated with the broader Gelato family. Sunset Sherbet contributes creamy citrus, berry sweetness, color, and a relaxed body influence, while Thin Mint GSC brings mint, earthy Cookies character, resin, spice, and a sharper cerebral dimension.

There is an important historical distinction, however. Gelato itself originated from Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint GSC and became famous through the work of Mario Guzman, better known as Sherbinskis, and the wider Cookie Fam circle. Numbered selections such as Gelato #33 and Bacio Gelato #41 became established names. In a 2024 interview discussing the original Gelato family, Guzman specifically said he does not recognize Gelato #45 as one of his original numbered selections. Therefore, it is more accurate to treat Barney’s Farm Gelato #45 as a documented modern selection from those parental genetics rather than claiming it is an authenticated original Sherbinskis #45 clone.

That distinction does not diminish the genetic character of the plant. Mature examples display many classic Gelato-family traits: compact flowers, lime and olive coloration, deep purple sugar leaves, amber pistils, and abundant sticky trichomes. Barney’s Farm also notes that plants can develop purple, red, and orange tones late in flowering.
Effects and Experience

The first stage often feels lighter than its indica percentage suggests. Mood rises, social interaction becomes easier, and humor can take on an exaggerated quality. Consumer data places relaxed, euphoric, and happy among the most commonly reported effects, while historical descriptions of Gelato 45 frequently emphasize its compatibility with social situations. Rather than generating frantic energy, the cerebral effect tends to produce an easygoing sense of engagement that works well for conversation, music, gaming, or an unstructured creative activity.

As the high develops, the physical side becomes more noticeable. The shoulders begin to loosen, movement feels less urgent, and the initial mental sparkle settles into a calmer rhythm. Moderate amounts may leave experienced consumers functional enough to remain socially active, while larger servings push the experience toward deeper relaxation. Appetite may increase, and a comfortable seat can become increasingly difficult to abandon.

Potency is the main reason to approach the cultivar gradually. Barney’s Farm lists THC potential up to 30%, although actual results depend on phenotype, cultivation, harvest timing, and laboratory methodology. Users report dizziness, dry mouth, and headache among possible adverse experiences. Consumers with limited THC tolerance should avoid assuming that creamy flavor means gentle effects.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers may appreciate this hybrid when they want psychological relaxation without beginning with immediate sedation. The early euphoric component can temporarily make stress or low mood feel less dominant, while the gradually developing body effect may reduce awareness of minor aches or muscular tension. Consumer reports most commonly associate Gelato 45 with anxiety, depression, and pain, although these are individual experiences rather than evidence of clinical effectiveness.

Later in the session, the stronger physical relaxation may make the cultivar more compatible with evening use. People who have difficulty winding down because of tension or discomfort may prefer this gradual transition compared with a marijuana strain that feels heavily sedating immediately. Higher servings are more likely to become sleepy or couch-oriented, though individual response varies considerably.

No controlled clinical research demonstrates that Gelato #45 specifically treats anxiety, depression, chronic pain, insomnia, or another condition. NCCIH notes that certain cannabinoid products may provide short-term benefit for some chronic pain conditions, while evidence concerning anxiety remains limited and depends on the cannabinoid preparation studied. High-THC cannabis can also produce unwanted psychological effects, so medical use should consider dose, individual sensitivity, medications, and professional guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness introduces the aroma, but earthier notes quickly complicate it. Barney’s Farm describes mint-chocolate ice cream and sweet berries alongside earthy pine, flowers, and skunky citrus. A properly cured flower may initially resemble berries folded into cream before pine resin, lemon rind, herbs, and damp earth become more apparent. Grinding the buds generally intensifies the sharper Cookies side and reduces the impression of straightforward dessert sweetness.

Caryophyllene, limonene, and humulene are prominent terpenes in Gelato 45 profile. Caryophyllene can emphasize pepper and dry spice, limonene supports citrus brightness, and humulene contributes woody or herbal depth. These compounds should not be considered a fixed formula for every harvest. Genetics establishes potential, but environment, nutrient management, maturity, drying, and curing determine how much of that aromatic chemistry survives into finished cannabis.

The inhale often begins with creamy berry, mint, and subtle sweetness. Citrus and floral notes appear through the middle, followed by a considerably drier exhale where pepper, pine, earth, and mild skunk become more prominent. That transition is what separates this cultivar from Gelato expressions dominated almost entirely by vanilla and fruit. Properly finished flower maintains enough sweetness to remain recognizably Gelato while preserving a surprisingly old-school earthy backbone.
Growing Information

Barney’s Farm describes Gelato #45 as a robust and forgiving plant that adapts to multiple cultivation techniques. Indoors, plants commonly reach about 100–120 centimeters, while outdoor specimens can stretch between approximately 180 and 250 centimeters. The breeder lists yields of roughly 650–750 grams per square meter indoors and as much as 1,500–2,000 grams per outdoor plant under highly favorable conditions. Those numbers represent optimized breeder potential rather than guaranteed harvests.

Its structure lends itself well to topping and low-stress training . Spreading branches early creates a more even canopy, improves light penetration, and prevents several upper colas from dominating production. Dense flowers become increasingly heavy as resin accumulates, so trellis netting or branch support can be useful during late bloom. Barney’s Farm describes mature buds as tightly compacted and heavily coated with swollen resin glands and trichomes.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 65–70 days, placing the plant close to nine or ten weeks. Outdoor harvest generally arrives during the first or second week of October. Because the flowers can become compact, late-flower humidity deserves careful control and strong air circulation should be maintained through the canopy. Purple and reddish coloration may intensify near maturity, but harvest timing should ultimately depend on trichome condition, calyx swelling, and overall flower development rather than leaf color.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Gelato #45?
The documented Barney’s Farm selection combines Sunset Sherbet with Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies, the same fundamental parental combination associated with the broader Gelato genetic family.
Who bred Gelato #45?

The version covered in this guide is bred by Barney’s Farm. The historical “#45” designation is complicated because Sherbinskis founder Mario Guzman has said he does not recognize Gelato #45 as one of his original numbered Gelato phenotypes.
Is Gelato #45 indica or sativa?
Barney’s Farm classifies its version as 60% indica and 40% sativa. The effect reflects that balance, beginning relatively euphoric and socially engaging before stronger physical relaxation develops.
What does Gelato #45 taste like?
Sweet berries and mint-chocolate cream form the sweeter side of the flavor, while citrus, earthy pine, flowers, pepper, and mild skunk add a drier finish.
How long does Gelato #45 take to flower?
Barney’s Farm lists an indoor flowering period of 65–70 days. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity during the first or second week of October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Gelato #45

Gelato #45 demonstrates how dramatically phenotype selection can reshape a familiar genetic pairing. Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint GSC provide the expected cream, berry, citrus, resin, and Cookies influence, but this expression pushes farther toward pine, earth, floral spice, and skunky complexity. The high develops in equally layered fashion, moving from cheerful cerebral engagement toward a calmer and more substantial physical state.

Its history also makes genetic sourcing especially important. The name is widely used in the cannabis market, yet its connection to the original Sherbinskis numbered Gelato family is disputed. For growers seeking reproducible cultivation information, Barney’s Farm provides a clearly documented modern version with strong production potential, a 65–70-day bloom, and substantial potency. For consumers, the attraction is simpler: this is Gelato with less emphasis on pure dessert sweetness and more of the earthy, piney depth that can make a famous genetic family feel surprisingly different.
